cases.description: a package whose protocols carry no @connection builds as before, on the one default connection
a package on comline@1 and datagram@2 with no @connection is unchanged and builds

packages.name: app

specification_version = 1

cases.description: @connection with one name puts each protocol in its own set
@connection with a list puts a protocol in several sets
a set's name is lowercase snake_case: letters, digits and underscores
one protocol annotated and another on a connection left out: nothing reaches a connection without a decision (fix: add @connection to Chat)
all or nothing holds across the package's schemas: a protocol in another schema, left out, is refused
a set named twice in one list is refused (fix: name it once)
an empty list names no set and is refused, not read as a protocol left out (fix: name at least one set)
a set is named by a bare identifier, never a string: @connection = "admin" is the annotation value error (core may hint to drop the quotes; the case holds the code only)
an annotation value that is neither a name nor a list of names, here a number, is the annotation value error
a lockstep datagram protocol runs on no connection, so it needn't be annotated once others are

packages.name: app
packages.config:
congregation app
specification_version = 1
handshake = "comline@2"
settings = { annotations = { framing = { allowed = true } } }

cases.description: @connection on a protocol that runs on no connection (the lockstep datagram) is refused

packages.name: app
packages.config:
congregation app
specification_version = 1
handshake = "comline@2"
settings = { annotations = { framing = { allowed = true } } }

cases.description: a set's name that isn't lowercase is refused (fix: admin)
a set's name ending in an underscore isn't lowercase snake_case and is refused (fix: admin)
a set's name with a doubled underscore isn't lowercase snake_case and is refused (fix: admin_api)
a set named like a Rust keyword builds: the generated name is loop_connection, never escaped
a set named like a TypeScript keyword, not a Rust one, builds
a set named like a Python keyword builds
a set named like a Lua keyword builds
a set named serve builds: the generated name is serve_connection, which is not the connection module's serve
a set named services builds: the generated name is services_connection, which is not the connection module's services
a set shop whose generated name shop_connection is the name of a schema is refused (fix: rename the set or the schema)
a set public whose generated name PublicConnection is the name of a protocol is refused (fix: rename the set or the protocol)
names that only look like the generated one are no collision: a schema shop_connections and a protocol PublicConn beside the sets shop and public
a set on comline@1 with datagram@2 is refused: the handshake hashes the whole schema and the framing numbers by position (the message says both)

packages.name: app
packages.config:
congregation app
specification_version = 1
wire = { framing = "datagram@2" }
handshake = "comline@1"

cases.description: a set on comline@1 is refused with any framing, here datagram@3: the handshake hashes the whole schema, so a change in one set would refuse every set (fix: comline@2)
a set on datagram@2 is refused with any handshake, here comline@2: the framing numbers protocols by position (fix: datagram@3)
